concepts.name: Series as labeled array
concepts.summary: Recall that a Series is a one-dimensional array of values paired with an index of labels and a single dtype.

concepts.name: DataFrame as table
concepts.summary: Explain that a DataFrame is a two-dimensional table of rows and columns where each column is a Series sharing a common index.

concepts.name: Reading files into DataFrames
concepts.summary: Load a CSV or similar file into a DataFrame and understand what the resulting object represents.

concepts.name: Inspecting a DataFrame
concepts.summary: Use head, shape, info, dtypes and describe to understand a dataset's size, columns, types and basic statistics.

concepts.name: Column selection
concepts.summary: Understand that selecting one column gives a Series while selecting a list of columns gives a DataFrame.

concepts.name: Index and column labels
concepts.summary: Recall that rows are identified by index labels and columns by names, and that both are accessible as attributes.

concepts.name: Column dtypes
concepts.summary: Understand that each column has a dtype such as int64, float64, object or datetime64 that determines which operations work.

misconceptions.text: A DataFrame is just a Python list of lists with no extra structure.
Selecting a single column with brackets returns a DataFrame.
Reading a CSV file keeps the file open and edits to the DataFrame change the file on disk.

concepts.name: Label versus position indexing
concepts.summary: Select rows and columns with loc by label and iloc by integer position, and know when each is appropriate.

concepts.name: Boolean mask filtering
concepts.summary: Filter rows with boolean conditions combined using &, | and ~ with parentheses, and with isin.

concepts.name: Creating and modifying columns
concepts.summary: Add or transform columns using vectorized arithmetic, assignment and rename or drop.

concepts.name: Missing value handling
concepts.summary: Detect missing values with isna and treat them with dropna or fillna depending on context.

concepts.name: Sorting and ranking
concepts.summary: Order rows by one or more columns and index labels, ascending or descending.

concepts.name: Summary statistics and counts
concepts.summary: Compute column aggregates and frequency counts, such as mean, sum, nunique and value_counts, to summarize data.

concepts.name: Writing data out
concepts.summary: Save a DataFrame to a file with control over the index and chosen columns.

concepts.name: Type conversion and string methods
concepts.summary: Convert column dtypes with astype and clean text columns using the str accessor.

misconceptions.text: Use and and or to combine multiple filter conditions on a DataFrame.
iloc slices include the end position just like loc label slices.
Methods like sort_values or dropna change the original DataFrame in place by default.

concepts.name: Split-apply-combine with groupby
concepts.summary: Group rows by one or more keys and apply aggregations to produce per-group summaries.

concepts.name: Multiple and named aggregations
concepts.summary: Apply several functions to different columns in one groupby with agg and name the outputs.

concepts.name: Merging and joining tables
concepts.summary: Combine DataFrames on keys with inner, left, right and outer joins and analyze how each affects the row count.

concepts.name: Concatenation of frames
concepts.summary: Stack DataFrames vertically or side by side and handle index alignment and mismatched columns.

concepts.name: Pivoting and reshaping
concepts.summary: Convert between wide and long layouts with pivot_table, melt, stack and unstack to suit an analysis.

concepts.name: Datetime handling
concepts.summary: Parse dates, extract components with the dt accessor, and compute time differences.

concepts.name: Index alignment in operations
concepts.summary: Predict how arithmetic between Series or DataFrames aligns on index labels and produces NaN for mismatches.

concepts.name: Data cleaning workflow
concepts.summary: Detect and resolve duplicates, inconsistent categories and outliers, and validate results systematically.

misconceptions.text: A merge always returns the same number of rows as the left table.
Groupby computes results immediately when called, before any aggregation is specified.
Arithmetic between two Series matches values by position, not by index label.

concepts.name: Transform and filter on groups
concepts.summary: Use transform, filter and apply on groups to add group-level features without collapsing rows, and choose among them.

concepts.name: Copy versus view semantics
concepts.summary: Diagnose when assignments modify the original or a copy, and avoid chained assignment by using loc or explicit copies.

concepts.name: Vectorization versus apply
concepts.summary: Evaluate when to use vectorized operations instead of apply or loops based on clarity and speed.

concepts.name: Memory-efficient dtypes
concepts.summary: Judge and apply categorical, nullable and downcast numeric dtypes to reduce memory use with correct semantics.

concepts.name: MultiIndex data manipulation
concepts.summary: Select, slice, reshape and reset hierarchical indexes produced by grouping and pivoting.

concepts.name: Time series resampling and windows
concepts.summary: Resample time series to other frequencies and compute rolling, expanding and shifted calculations.

concepts.name: Method chaining pipelines
concepts.summary: Structure readable, reproducible transformations as method chains using assign, query and pipe.

concepts.name: Merge validation and diagnostics
concepts.summary: Check key uniqueness and unmatched rows during merges to detect silent row duplication or loss.

misconceptions.text: Using apply with a row-wise function is just as fast as a vectorized operation.
Chained indexing such as df[mask]['col'] = value reliably updates the original DataFrame.
Converting every string column to category is always beneficial regardless of cardinality.

concepts.name: Performance profiling and optimization
concepts.summary: Profile pipelines to find bottlenecks and choose between vectorization, indexing, dtype changes and algorithmic restructuring.

concepts.name: Scaling beyond memory
concepts.summary: Evaluate chunked reading, column selection, columnar formats and alternative engines when data exceeds memory.

concepts.name: Designing reusable data pipelines
concepts.summary: Design modular, tested and idempotent transformation functions with explicit schemas for production use.

concepts.name: Data validation and schema contracts
concepts.summary: Create automated checks for types, ranges, uniqueness and referential integrity that fail loudly on bad data.

concepts.name: Custom extensions and accessors
concepts.summary: Extend pandas with custom accessors or extension types where built-in behavior does not fit a domain.

concepts.name: Choosing pandas versus alternatives
concepts.summary: Judge when pandas, SQL, NumPy or other dataframe engines best suit a task based on scale, semantics and team context.

concepts.name: Reproducible statistical analysis workflows
concepts.summary: Build analyses that are deterministic and auditable, handling missing data, bias and sampling choices explicitly.

misconceptions.text: If a dataset fits in memory, pandas performance is never a concern.
Pandas is always the best tool for any tabular task, so alternatives are unnecessary.
Passing a few visual spot checks is enough to validate a data pipeline's output.
